Role Overview
The Enterprise Architecture Manager is a strategic senior technical leader responsible for defining, directing, and governing the enterprise target state architecture, technology portfolio lifecycle, and modernization roadmap across Citi's global technology estate.
In this role, you will lead the transformation of application architecture governance, software and infrastructure inventory management, data analytics capabilities, and the operationalization of next-generation enterprise AI patterns. Operating at the intersection of business strategy, enterprise architecture, and emerging AI technologies, you will partner with senior technology, risk, compliance, and business leaders to drive enterprise-wide modernization programs, elevate data quality, mitigate technical debt, and ensure continuous regulatory and audit readiness.
Key Responsibilities
1. Enterprise Architecture Governance & Strategic Modernization
- Target State Architecture (TSA) & Blueprints: Define, govern, and maintain the Enterprise Target State Architecture, Transition Roadmaps, and Reference Architectures across all domains: Business, Data, Application, Technology, and Security (BDATS) .
- Architecture Governance Framework: Operationalize Architecture Review Boards (ARBs), establish enterprise Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), and enforce adherence to standard frameworks (e.g., TOGAF 10, BIAN ).
- Application & Infrastructure Portfolio Management (APM): Oversee global application inventory, software asset lifecycles, and CMDB data fidelity to eliminate architectural debt, manage obsolescence, and support cloud migration and legacy modernization initiatives.
- Root Cause & Impact Analysis: Conduct in-depth technical investigations, Root Cause Analyses (RCA), and structural impact assessments on core operating platforms to engineer proactive systemic guardrails.
2. Multi-Agent Systems, Autonomous Engineering & AI Architecture
- Autonomous AI & Developer Platforms (Devin AI / AI Engineering): Architect and integrate autonomous software engineering agents and AI coding platforms (e.g., Devin AI , GitHub Copilot Workspace, Cursor, Claude Code) into the enterprise Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), establishing secure sandboxing, verification pipelines, architectural compliance gates, and automated code review guardrails.
- Agentic Orchestration & Patterns: Architect enterprise-grade pattern-based multi-agent systems utilizing frameworks such as Salesforce Agentic Architecture, LangGraph/AutoGen, and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) orchestration patterns (Supervisor-Worker, Hierarchical Planning, ReAct).
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration: Define and implement Model Context Protocol (MCP) standards and secure tool-calling interfaces to decouple LLMs and autonomous agents from backend enterprise services, databases, and microservices.
- Knowledge Graphs & Semantic Ontologies: Architect Enterprise Architecture Knowledge Graphs (EAKG) using open semantic ontologies

The Vice President (VP) / Senior Software Engineer – Technical Remediation & Enablement Lead is a hands-on, code-level technical specialist responsible for driving the direct remediation of software vulnerabilities across enterprise application teams. This individual contributor / team-level technical lead works alongside application developers and contractor engineers to fix static code vulnerabilities (SAST), patch vulnerable software dependencies (SCA/third-party libraries), containerize workloads, and streamline local build/release pipelines to achieve same-day vulnerability hotfix and deployment capabilities .
This role combines active software engineering (writing/refactoring code and debugging pipelines) with technical enablement, guiding squad developers on how to adopt internal security and build tools, resolve tricky dependency conflicts, and package applications into modern containers for rapid, low-risk production releases.

Every product Databricks ships has to be priced, contracted, rated and billed before it can earn a dollar. Built to set the gold standard for integrated AI infrastructure

 

Crux AI is a newly formed, U.S.-based integrated AI infrastructure company created to remove the physical and operational constraints on consequential AI ambitions. Crux brings together power, high-density data centers, TPU silicon, networking, orchestration software, and ongoing operations as one integrated system.

 

Crux is being capitalized to plan every layer together, develop each one to demanding standards, and operate the whole system with efficiency and reliability. That gives hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, enterprises, and AI-native companies greater freedom to pursue the AI they are here to create.

 

What you'll do



You will define how Crux runs its TPU fleet, and build it so that AI agents, not people, do most of the operating.



Reporting to our CTPO, you will own the telemetry that ties our facilities, clusters, and network together, the incident and change processes that govern them, and the autonomous systems that detect, triage, and remediate failures before a customer notices.



As the first leader of this function, you will write the operating model, hire the team, and take it from the first Stage 1 build to fleet scale, partnering with Compute, Network Engineering, Facility Operations, Security, Customer Success, and Google.



In this role, you will:

 - Own one telemetry and event pipeline across power, cooling, TPU hosts, interconnect, and the control plane, with the correlation to tell a failing pump from a failing chip from a failing job.

 - Build AI agents that triage alerts, run runbooks, drain and requeue workloads, and initiate RMAs with Google, with a measured share of work closed with zero human touch.

 - Set SLOs and error budgets for every Crux service, and run the incident, postmortem, and change process that holds the fleet to them.

 - Stand up 24/7 fleet operations where agents handle repeat failures and people handle novel ones, then turn them into automation.

 - Hire and develop SRE, fleet operations, and AI tooling leaders.



Signals of success



After 90 days in this role:

 - Published the AI Ops operating model: SLOs, on-call and escalation, incident process, and ownership boundaries with adjacent teams.

 - Mapped every critical failure mode for the first build to a signal, an alert, a runbook, and an owner.



After 6 months:

 - Taken the first Stage 1 cluster into production with SLOs met.

 - Built, hands-on, AI agents the team uses every day, with a measured share of incidents resolved without human intervention.



After 1 year:

 - Run a multi-site fleet where most operational work executes autonomously, with measurable gains in availability, recovery time, and cost per chip.

 - Become a reason strong SRE and operations engineers choose Crux.



Experiences, attributes and mindset that indicate a good match



Experiences

 - 15+ years in large-scale infrastructure operations, SRE, or network op

A Director within the Nordstrom Technology organization helps create an inspiring workplace where talented people are empowered to drive customer experiences and business results. This key leader influences the organization through servant leadership and leads with empathy. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is seeking a Director of Applied Science to lead the Responsible AI Applied Science team. This leader will define and execute the scientific and technical strategy for building the next generation of Responsible AI technologies that enable customers to safely and reliably deploy multimodal generative AI models and agentic systems at enterprise scale.

The Responsible AI Applied Science team advances research and develops cutting-edge technologies for guardrailing multimodal generative AI models and AI agents . The team's work spans models and applications that reason over and generate across modalities—including text, images, audio, video, and combinations of these modalities . Research areas include content safety and moderation, prompt injection and adversarial attacks, privacy and PII protection, hallucination and grounding, reliability, formal verification, and emerging approaches for governing and constraining agent behavior.

As generative AI becomes increasingly multimodal, safety challenges extend beyond individual prompts and responses to the interactions between modalities, models, tools, and agents. The team develops new techniques for understanding and mitigating these risks while building guardrails that can operate effectively across diverse models, modalities, and enterprise use cases.

This is a senior scientific leadership role at the intersection of research, product, and engineering . The Director will lead a team of applied scientists, establish the team's research and product roadmap, and translate advances in multimodal Responsible AI into differentiated capabilities for OCI customers. Our mission is to return the atmosphere to 280 ppm CO₂. We convert excess inedible biomass into carbon-rich bio-oil and inject it into underground storage for permanent carbon removal. At scale, we can use bio-oil to make fossil-free iron.
